key_insight: The paper combines data storytelling with interpretable machine learning to make AI decisions understandable to non-experts while limiting exposure of sensitive data and model internals.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical framework for turning model explanations into accessible narratives, which is useful for deployable, user-facing AI systems in high-stakes settings.
method: Defines data storytelling for interpretable machine learning using the DIST Pyramid.
Introduces an I-P-O Model to describe how storytelling and explanations interact.
Builds a what-if/why-not explanation architecture with data desensitization and SHAP plus LLM-generated ABT narratives.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the what-if and why-not stories more comprehensible, with significantly higher accessibility than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful narrative generation and desensitization; inaccurate storytelling or incomplete privacy protection could mislead users or leak sensitive information.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
